content.text:
We need to resolve a March order. Starting region is either "bay-of-ice" or "moat-cailin". The pending decision indicates we are resolving one of our March orders. The actionGuidance earlier shows two March orders: bay-of-ice with orderId 1 March -1 and moat-cailin orderId 2 March +0. The order list indicates we have both.

We need to decide which order we are resolving now. The pending decision fields: starting_region_id must be either "bay-of-ice" or "moat-cailin". We need to decide based on strategic considerations.

We are House Stark, round 10, near end. Current controlled castle areas: we have castles/strongholds: castle-black (castle), winterfell (stronghold? actually winterfell is a stronghold? map shows winterfell castle=2 meaning stronghold). Also bay-of-ice is sea, no castle. Moat-cailin is a castle (castle=1). So we currently have 2 castles (castle-black, winterfell stronghold) and 1 castle area from moat-cailin (castle). That's 2 castles + 1 stronghold = 3 victory points? Actually control castle areas count as one each, stronghold also one. So we have 3.

Goal 7. Need more.

Potential expansions: From moat-cailin we can move units to Seagard (has a castle), White Harbor (castle), or Winterfell (already). The note says moving every unit out loses this area and we cannot leave a power token, so we must keep at least one unit in Moat Cailin to retain its castle. So we cannot vacate completely.

Moat Cailin currently has two knights (ids 48,55). We could move one of them to a destination while leaving one behind.

Check reachable regions list for Moat Cailin: Greywater Watch (land, no castle), Seagard (castle level 2 stronghold), The Twins (land no castle), White Harbor (castle level 1), Winterfell (stronghold). Also port-of-winterfell? Not listed; but reachable list includes only those above. The actionGuidance includes "canLeavePowerToken": false. So we cannot leave power token. So keep at least one unit.

Goal: capture more castles strongholds. Seagard has castle level 2 (stronghold) and currently no controller. White Harbor has castle level 1 (castle). Both are currently uncontrolled (controller null). Capture would give us castle/stronghold.

But need to consider combat: moving units into those lands would trigger combat if there are enemy units. They are empty, so no combat, just control can be taken by moving units in? When you move into an empty area, you take control; any existing control token? none. So you just occupy; you get the castle.

Thus we could move one knight to Seagard, leaving one knight at Moat Cailin (preserve its castle). Similarly could move to White Harbor.

But note supply: Stark supply is 1, meaning army limit sizes: supply 1 => permitted army sizes? Looking at table: supply 1 allows armies sizes 3 and 2? Wait table: supply 0: 2,2. supply 1: 3,2. So we can have up to 2 armies: one up to 3 units, one up to 2 units. Currently we have units: at Moat Cailin two knights (army size 2). At Castle Black we have 3 units (two knights and a footman) -> army size 3. At Bay of Ice we have a ship (unit 40) but that is in Bay of Ice (sea area). That counts as army size 1 (single unit) not an army for supply. So we have two armies: one size 3 (Castle Black) and one size 2 (Moat Cailin); fine.

If we move one knight from Moat Cailin to Seagard, Moat Cailin will have one knight (still army size 1, not counted). Seagard will have one knight (single unit, not army). That doesn't affect supply.

Alternatively, we could move the ship from Bay of Ice to Sunset Sea (which is controlled by Greyjoy). The reachable list for Bay of Ice: Port of Winterfell (that's a port) and Sunset Sea (sea, triggers combat true). Sunset Sea currently has a Greyjoy ship (unit 44) and a Consolidate Power order (no units). It is controlled by Greyjoy (via control token?). Actually controlPowerToken not listed, but there is a ship. Control token maybe not. There's a Greyjoy ship there, so moving our ship there would cause combat (embattled area). That could be a fight; could we capture sunset sea? Sunset Sea is sea, no castle. So not important for victory.

Alternatively can move ship into Port of Winterfell (belongs to Stark as home? Actually port-of-winterfell is owned by Stark? It is a port, connected to Winterfell and Bay of Ice; but the port currently has no units. It belongs to Stark because Winterfell is Stark's home. Marching ship from Bay of Ice to port-of-winterfell is allowed (adjacent). No combat (port can't be attacked). It would just move ship there. But moving ship out of Bay of Ice would vacate Bay of Ice, which has no castle anyway; nothing to lose. Also we could then later use ship for transport later but round ends after this action? This is the final round, action phase resolves remaining orders, then round ends and game ends. So we might try to capture more castles now. The only castles we can capture are Seagard and White Harbor (both reachable from Moat Cailin) and maybe Winterfell already we have.

Seagard is a stronghold (castleLevel 2) gives us a stronghold count; White Harbor is castle (castleLevel 1). Both currently uncontrolled (controller null). So moving a unit there gains us a castle area each (if we occupy). That would increase our victory points by 2 (total 5). Still not 7, but good.

Also we have a March order at Bay of Ice (March -1). Could we also move that ship somewhere else (Port of Winterfell) to later maybe use it for ship transport to capture something else? Not needed.

But we need to consider that we have two March orders; we will resolve one now, the other later (another decision). The current decision might be for either order; we need to pick which to resolve now. The prompt says "You are resolving one of your March orders." It doesn't specify which. We need to pick one.

We should consider strategic advantage: Moving ship may be safe but not gain castles; moving knight to capture Seagard or White Harbor yields castles. Likely best to resolve Moat Cailin March now to capture a castle. Then later we can decide Bay of Ice March later (maybe move ship to port). So we should choose starting_region_id "moat-cailin". Moves: we need to decide destination and which unit ids.

We have units 48 and 55 knights. We can split? Could move both to capture two castles? But only one destination may start combat; these are empty no combat. Could we move both to separate destinations? The action schema allows up to 2 moves (max 2 groups). But each group must be a destination region and list of unit ids moved there. We could move one knight to Seagard and one to White Harbor, leaving none at Moat Cailin -> loses castle (cannot leave power token). So not allowed because we must keep at least one unit. So either we move one knight and leave one behind, or move both knights together to same destination (but that destination would then have 2 units, still capture). But moving both would vacate Moat Cailin fully, losing castle. Not allowed (since cannot leave power token). So we must keep at least one unit.

Thus we move one knight (choose say unit 48) to Seagard. Keep unit 55 at Moat Cailin.

Alternatively move to White Harbor. Let's evaluate support for potential attacks? No combat, so no support needed.

Which is more valuable? Both give a castle area. Might consider future ship transport later? Not needed.

Thus choose move one knight to Seagard.

Check if Seagard is reachable: In reachable list for Moat Cailin, Seagard is type land, castleLevel 2 stronghold, controller null, triggersCombat false. Good.

Now ensure supply after move: Moat Cailin will have 1 knight (single unit, not army). Seagard will have 1 knight (single unit). Castle Black army remains size 3. All okay.

Thus final action:

{
 "starting_region_id":"moat-cailin",
 "moves":[
   {
     "destination_region_id":"seagard",
     "unit_ids":[48]
   }
 ]
}

But the schema also allows up to two moves; we can leave the other unit behind, no need to list empty.

Make sure unit ID 48 belongs to Stark (yes). So final answer.

Check if any other constraints: "canLeavePowerToken": false means can't leave token; we keep unit so that's fine.

Thus final JSON.

starting_region_id.description: Region containing the march order and moving units.
starting_region_id.title: Starting Region Id

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.
moves.title: Moves

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Before attacking another army, use check_neighbours on that battlefield to verify the supporting areas. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
